title: Sale Day
tagline: Two big sales a year, and about fifteen rounds of price increases a year.
what: I run the website and email side of the big sales and every price change in between, from working out the prices to switching them back off.
does: Plan the two big yearly sales: dates, discount levels, price lists
Work out every sale price and load it everywhere it shows
Build the sale page, banners and countdowns with the contract designer
Draft, preview and schedule the sale emails
Switch the sale on, and take it down again in a day
Set quantity discounts, bundle deals and free-shipping offers
Run price increases across every kit and option, with a before-and-after record
Run dealer prices, coupon codes, payment plans and pre-orders

solved.problem: Price increases hit parts that live inside many kits and options, so a one-part change could leave a dozen products wrong.
solved.did: I made the tool spread a change to every kit and option that contains the part, kept the endings consistent, and added a baseline so increases never stack on top of earlier ones.
solved.ended: A single round turned four part changes into dozens of price updates, every one applied and checked.

solved.problem: The price a rep quoted and the price on the website had to agree, every time.
solved.did: I lined up every place a price gets set, so every kind of deal counts the same way everywhere, and a rep's discount gets a quick yes or no before it goes out.
solved.ended: A quote matches the website for that day.

solved.problem: Dealers worked from a wholesale price spreadsheet that went stale.
solved.did: I settled who counts as a dealer, in one rule every report uses, and built a page where dealers sign in and see their price.
solved.ended: The spreadsheet is retired, and every dealer got the new page.

solved.problem: The team found pricing mistakes by chance, such as one product priced under its newer version.
solved.did: I fixed each one as it was reported and corrected the pricing rules behind it.
solved.ended: The team can report a price and trust it gets sorted.

tools.name: Price changer
tools.line: change a price once and it reaches every kit and option, with a history and a clean undo. Used by me and purchasing.

tools.name: Sale switch
tools.line: turns a whole sale on and off by button or timer.

tools.name: Coupon maker
tools.line: the whole customer service team creates and turns off codes on their own.

tools.name: Dealer price page
tools.line: dealers sign in and see their price.

worksWith: Leadership, customer service, purchasing, accounting, a contract designer, a developer.
story: Black Friday sales came in over 60% higher than the year before, and I took the sale down in one day. Leadership set the discounts; I worked out the prices and ran the websites and email.
The first sale I ran meant changing prices across both sites by hand, then spending days taking it down.
For the next Black Friday I put every sale price in one file, worked out the savings and added a preview and a single on-off switch. I could see the sale before customers did.

By spring, that file had grown into a price tool with a sale planner. I tested it on a real price increase, checked every product, then ran the whole spring sale on it. That sale came down in a day too.
credit: The job, plus the tools I built for it
